messages:
Maya Patel: FYI reproducible hang in Go quickstart generator sample when cancelling ctx during streaming. Repro: start stream, cancel parent ctx after ~200ms, goroutines climb and process doesn't exit cleanly.

Maya Patel: Snippet from sample:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 150*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
stream, _ := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, model, opts)
for stream.Next() { fmt.Println(stream.Token()) }
if err := stream.Err(); err != nil { log.Println("stream error:", err) }
```

Chris Nguyen: Two suspects: transport requests missing req.WithContext, or an auth refresh goroutine that ignores ctx.

Maya Patel: Sample helper spins a tiny token refresher that auto-retries on 401.

Sasha Ivanov: If retry/backoff uses time.Sleep without checking ctx.Done() we'll leak goroutines.

Priyanka Rao: Also check that generator.Stream wires ctx into the http request so the underlying read unblocks.

Chris Nguyen: Grep shows http.NewRequest(...) then go doRetry(req) which spawns attempts writing to a channel without honoring ctx.

Alex Gomez: I reproduced with pprof; goroutines stuck in backoff sleep. Uploaded small repro gist.

Priyanka Rao: Fix plan: 1) use req = req.WithContext(ctx) for transport 2) make retry/backoff ctx-aware (select on ctx.Done) 3) expose Stream.Close()/Cancel() in SDK and add example.

Sasha Ivanov: Docs + quickstart note: warn that background refreshers can keep demo apps alive; prefer ctx-aware sleep in examples.

Alex Gomez: I'll open PR with the fixes and docs update (ETA EOD tomorrow).

devex-bot: CI queued for quickstart tests.

Maya Patel: Thanks — assigning follow-ups in GH issue #789.
